---
title: "Run from a TOML file"
---

A TOML file records a run, so you can keep it in Git and repeat it exactly. The same
file works on the command line and in Python (`MeshSpec`).

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: false
import sys
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pyogrio.raw
import shapely
from shapely import Point, box

workdir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
gpkg = workdir / "model.gpkg"


def write(layer, geometries, fields=None):
    fields = fields or {}
    pyogrio.raw.write(
        gpkg,
        shapely.to_wkb(np.asarray(geometries, dtype=object)),
        field_data=list(fields.values()),
        fields=list(fields),
        crs="EPSG:28992",
        geometry_type="Polygon",
        layer=layer,
        driver="GPKG",
    )


write("modelgebied", [box(155_000, 463_000, 155_640, 463_480)])
write("verfijning", [Point(155_250, 463_240).buffer(60)], {"refinement": np.array([2])})
write("water", [Point(155_520, 463_330).buffer(35)])

run_toml = """\
cell_size = 32.0
transition_rows = [1, 2]
water_removal = "centre"
output = "mesh_net.nc"

[domain]
path = "model.gpkg"
layer = "modelgebied"

[[refinement_areas]]
path = "model.gpkg"
layer = "verfijning"
level = "refinement"   # a column name, or one integer level

[[water_areas]]
path = "model.gpkg"
layer = "water"
"""
(workdir / "run.toml").write_text(run_toml, encoding="utf-8")
```

## The file

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
print(f"```toml\n{run_toml}```")
```

Paths are relative to the TOML file. Other keys: `crs` (for layers without CRS),
`origin = [x, y]` (a lattice point) and more `[[refinement_areas]]` or `[[water_areas]]`
tables. An unknown key or an invalid value is an error that names the key and the reason.

## Generate on the command line

```bash
refined-quads generate run.toml
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
from refined_quads.cli import main

main(["generate", str(workdir / "run.toml")])
```

Options override the file: `-o other_net.nc`, `--cell-size 25`,
`--transition-rows 1 1`, `--water-removal inside`, `--crs EPSG:28992`,
`--origin 155000 463000`, and `-v` prints the progress.

The exit code is 0 when the mesh is written, 1 when the run failed (the orthogonality
repair did not close; then `mesh_net_raw.nc` and `mesh_net_problems.gpkg` are written
next to the output) and 2 for invalid input or arguments.

## Look at a mesh

`refined-quads info` shows the lattice, the cells per refinement level and the checks of
any UGRID file, also a D-HYDRO net file with a 1D network:

```bash
refined-quads info mesh_net.nc
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
main(["info", str(workdir / "mesh_net.nc")])
```

## The same in Python

```{python}
from refined_quads import MeshSpec

spec = MeshSpec.from_toml(workdir / "run.toml")
quad_mesh = spec.replace(cell_size=25.0).generate()
print(quad_mesh)
```
